legend: Abhinav is a scientist who works in the field of perfect arrays. What's a perfect array you ask, let me explain —
A perfect array of size n%%ZSMJ0%% is made by performing n%%ZSMJ1%% perfect operations on an empty array and –

The p%%ZSMJ2%%-th perfect operation involves choosing a random integer q%%ZSMJ3%% between 1%%ZSMJ4%% and p%%ZSMJ5%% (1≤q≤p)%%ZSMJ6%%, and inserting it in the q%%ZSMJ7%%-th position. So, for instance if before the p%%ZSMJ8%%-th operation array was like A1,A2...Aq−1,Aq,Aq+1....Ap−1%%ZSMJ9%%, then after the p%%ZSMJ10%%-th operation array becomes A1,A2...Aq−1,q,Aq,Aq+1,Aq+2....Ap−1%%ZSMJ11%%.

Harsh wants to become Abhinav's assistant and to check Harsh's intelligence, Abhinav gives him an array Arr%%ZSMJ12%% of size n%%ZSMJ13%% and asks him if it is a perfect array or not. And if Arr%%ZSMJ14%% is a perfect array, Harsh is required to give the sequence of n%%ZSMJ15%% operations that built up Arr%%ZSMJ16%%.
Harsh is too dumb to solve this and asks for your help.
input: The first line of input contains an integer n%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤n≤200)%%ZSMJ18%% – the size of given array.
The next line of input contains n%%ZSMJ19%% integers, Arr1,Arr2,....Arrn%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤Arri≤N)%%ZSMJ21%% – the elements of given array.
output: If the given array is not perfect then print "NO".
Else, in the first line print "YES" and in the next line print the sequence of n%%ZSMJ22%% operations that built up the array.
note: 1%%ZSMJ23%%-st operation – Add 1%%ZSMJ24%% at 1%%ZSMJ25%%-st index. Array becomes [1]%%ZSMJ26%%
2%%ZSMJ27%%-nd operation – Add 1%%ZSMJ28%% at 1%%ZSMJ29%%-st index. Array becomes [1,1]%%ZSMJ30%%
3%%ZSMJ31%%-rd operation – Add 2%%ZSMJ32%% at 2%%ZSMJ33%%-nd index. Array becomes [1,2,1]%%ZSMJ34%%
In the second sample testcase, there is no possible sequence of operations that can form the array [2,2]%%ZSMJ35%%.
